subject: Craftly.ai — renewal health checkpoint & roll-forward options
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connell <liam.oconnell@craftly.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 10 Feb 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Craftly.ai — renewal health checkpoint & roll-forward options

Hi Liam,

Quick check-in ahead of your March 1 renewal. We pulled a brief health snapshot and two pragmatic paths that align to Craftly's usage profile and latency goals — attaching the Q4 usage export and token economics by model. TL;DR: your run rate averaged ~1.9B tokens/month in Q4, with a short-lived peak of 3.4B in late Nov that drove overage exposure on our hosted plan. The core drivers were an increase in sampling for the assistant flow and a temporary batch job that reindexed onboarding data.

Two suggested roll-forward options we can operationalize quickly:

1) Right-size commit + term (recommended)
   - 12-month commit: +15% token baseline (covers normal growth + 1x Nov-style spike)
   - Price: current unit price less 8% (applies to committed tokens)
   - Predictability: removes overage surprises and unlocks burst credits for controlled spikes

2) Flexible commit + burst credits (quick stop-gap)
   - Maintain current commit; add a pool of burst credits you draw from during peaks
   - No long-term price change; good if you expect the Nov spike to be one-off

Operational notes we recommend before finalizing: enable KV prefix caching for the assistant flows (estimated 10–15% token reduction) and switch a subset of mid-tier models to int8 quantized variants; Naomi's team has a short testing checklist that should be non-disruptive.

Request: can you confirm which path you prefer by Friday, Feb 24? If helpful, Rishi can put together the formal pricing sheet and a 48–72 hour Dedicated trial window for a single GPU pool to validate latency and cost assumptions.

Files attached: craftly_usage_q4-2027.pdf, token_econ_by_model.xlsx

Thanks —
Tessa
Director, Renewals — Redwood Inference
(t) 415-555-0124

From: Liam O'Connell <liam.oconnell@craftly.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 11 Feb 2028 11:05:43 -0000
Subject: Re: Craftly.ai — renewal health checkpoint & roll-forward options

Thanks Tessa — appreciate the snapshot. A couple quick clarifying Qs before we pick a path:

- If we go with the 12-month commit and still see a Nov-scale spike, how do burst credits interact with overage protection? Do we get an automatic temporary pool or is it manual?
- Can you confirm the SLA credit window for an incident at the scale we saw in November (we experienced ~350ms tail latency increase for ~4 hours)?

Sophie (our infra lead) is OOO next week but I should be able to confirm direction after I sync with her. If there's a simple way to run a Dedicated pool for 48–72 hours to validate latency we'd be interested.

— Liam
Head of Product — Craftly.ai
liam.oconnell@craftly.ai

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connell <liam.oconnell@craftly.ai>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 12 Feb 2028 08:30:21 -0800
Subject: Re: Craftly.ai — renewal health checkpoint & roll-forward options

Hi Liam — quick add from pricing side; attaching a formal proposal (craftly_proposal_v2.pdf) with explicit examples. Short answers to your questions first:

- Burst credits and overage protection: in the 12-month commit we bake-in a 10% emergency burst pool by default; you only draw from it if configured autoscale triggers. Overage beyond committed + burst pool is billed at the standard overage rate unless we agree a capped overage clause in the contract.
- SLA credits: for a one-off tail latency event similar to November, our standard SLA gives a pro-rata service credit; for Commit Option B (24-month) we can include a 1x SLA-makeup credit for qualifying incidents in the year of the renewal.

Pricing highlights from the proposal:
- Option A (12mo, +15% commit): committed unit price = $0.00118/1k tokens (8% off current) + built-in 10% burst pool.
- Option B (24mo, +10% commit): committed unit price = $0.00098/1k tokens (22% off current) + 15% burst pool + 1x annual SLA credit clause.

If you want, we can provision a 72-hr Dedicated pool from Feb 21–24 to validate latency/cost tradeoffs; that runs under a short-term MSA addendum (no change to your live traffic unless you flip routing). Let me know preferred dates and I'll raise the internal ticket.

Rishi
Account Executive — Redwood Inference

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connell <liam.oconnell@craftly.ai>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Feb 2028 16:45:10 -0800
Subject: Re: Craftly.ai — renewal health checkpoint & roll-forward options

Hi Liam — adding a short operational checklist from CS to make the Dedicated trial and long-term roll-forward low friction:

1) Pre-trial environment snapshot (we'll export current prefix KV hit rates and batching histograms) — 1–2 hours work on your side.
2) Provisioning: we'll spin a single GPU pool with identical model variants you currently use. Traffic will be mirrored (read-only) unless you opt to switch.
3) KV and batching: enable prefix caching for assistant flows during test; Naomi can push a non-invasive config that reduces token churn (expect ~10% token savings).
4) Post-trial report: latency percentiles (P50/P95/P99), token consumption delta, and modeled monthly cost if migrated to Dedicated under Option B.

If you accept the 72-hr trial, Naomi and I will run the pre-trial checklist the week prior (expect 2–3 working hours from your infra). Happy to run the 72-hr window Feb 21–24 as Rishi suggested.

Best,
Monica Patel
Customer Success Manager — Redwood Inference

From: Liam O'Connell <liam.oconnell@craftly.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 17 Feb 2028 09:00:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Craftly.ai — renewal health checkpoint & roll-forward options

Thanks all — Sophie and I reviewed the options. We're inclined to go with Option B (24mo, +10% commit) contingent on two items: (1) a 72-hour Dedicated trial for a single GPU pool (Feb 21–24) to validate P95/P99 latency improvements, and (2) a written clause in the renewal that includes a one-time SLA makeup credit for any qualifying incident within the first 12 months.

If those two items are included, we can sign the amendment and move forward. Rishi — please send updated proposal with contract language around the SLA credit and runoff for the Dedicated trial.

Onward —
Liam
Head of Product — Craftly.ai
